Technology Limited | native_name = {{lang|zh|新能源科技有限公司}} | logo = ATL_logo.PNG | founder = [[Robin Zeng]] | founded = {{start date and age|1999}} | hq_location_city = [[Hong Kong]] | traded_as = | key_people = {{Unbulleted list | Robin Zeng | [[Huang Shilin]] | Joe Kit Chu Lam }} | industry = {{Unbulleted list | [[Energy storage]] | [[Battery recycling]] }} | num_employees = 42,000 (2022){{Cite web |title=TDK 2022 Annual Report|url=https://www.tdk.com/system/files/ir_library_report_pdf_lib40370_en.pdf |access-date=31 March 2024 }} | revenue = {{nowrap|Over {{JPY|500 billion|link=yes}} (FY2023)}} | net_income = {{nowrap|Over {{JPY|90 billion}} (FY2023)}} | website = {{URL|https://www.atlbattery.com/}} }} [[File:Redmi Note 8 - Ningde Amperex Technology BN46-4924.jpg|thumb|Li-ion Polymer battery Ningde Amperex Technology BN46]] '''Amperex Technology Limited (ATL)''' is a [[electric battery|battery]] manufacturing company founded in 1999 by [[Robin Zeng]]. The company specializes in the research, development, and manufacturing of rechargeable [[Lithium-ion battery|lithium-ion]] and [[Lithium polymer battery|lithium-ion polymer]] batteries. ATL is notable for supplying batteries used in mobile devices, including smartphones, laptops, and digital cameras, sourcing their products to tech companies such as [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] and [[Samsung]].{{Cite web |last=Wang |first=Jennifer |date=2021-05-03 |title=This Chinese Battery Company Has Produced More Billionaires Than Google Or Facebook |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jenniferwang/2021/05/03/this-chinese-battery-company-has-produced-more-billionaires-than-google-or-facebook/ |access-date= |website=Forbes |language=en}}{{Cite news |last1=Martin |first1=Timothy W. |last2=McKinnon |first2=John D. |date=2017-01-20 |title=Samsung Investigation Blames Battery Size for Galaxy Note 7 Fires |language=en-US |work=Wall Street Journal |url=http://www.wsj.com/articles/samsung-investigation-blames-battery-size-for-galaxy-note-7-fires-1484906193 |access-date= |issn=0099-9660}}{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Stan |date=2022-04-28 |title=Samsung considering using ATL's batteries for new foldable phones |url=http://thelec.net/news/articleView.html?idxno=4010 |access-date= |website=THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media |language=ko}} ATL is headquartered in [[Hong Kong]] and has production facilities in [[Dongguan]] and [[Ningde]], China, as well as a lithium-ion battery cell plant in [[Haryana]], India, opened in 2025.{{Cite news |last=Haidar |first=Faizan |date=2020-08-12 |title=Japanese firm Amperex Technology Limited acquires 180-acre at Rs 550 crore in Haryana |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/japanese-firm-amperex-technology-limited-acquires-180-acre-at-rs-550-crore-in-haryana/articleshow/77488247.cms |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}{{Cite news |date=2025-09-04 |title=Vaishnaw inaugurates lithium-ion battery plant in Haryana, says "India on path to self-reliance in electronics" |url=https://ddnews.gov.in/en/vaishnaw-inaugurates-lithium-ion-battery-plant-in-haryana-says-india-on-path-to-self-reliance-in-electronics/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |work=DD News}} == Company history == Zeng Yuqun, more commonly known as [[Robin Zeng]], founded ATL in 1999.{{Cite web |last=Rathi |first=Akshat |date=2019-04-03 |title=The inside story of how CATL became the world's largest electric-vehicle battery company |url=https://qz.com/1585662/how-catl-became-the-worlds-biggest-electric-car-battery-company |website=Quartz |language=en}} Operating from the company headquarters in Hong Kong, Zeng acquired technology licenses from US companies to make batteries for laptops and MP3 players. In its early years the company made batteries only for portable consumer electronics.{{Cite web |date=2019-04-03 |title=The inside story of how CATL became the world’s largest electric-vehicle battery company |url=https://qz.com/1585662/how-catl-became-the-worlds-biggest-electric-car-battery-company |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=Quartz |language=en}} Two years after establishment, ATL was able to produce batteries for 1 million devices. In the aftermath of this success, the company was acquired by [[TDK]] in 2005.Tyler-Dudley, Davis, et al. "[http://www.johnandrewferguson.com/documents/batteryking.pdf CATL: China's Battery King.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230716184805/https://www.johnandrewferguson.com/documents/batteryking.pdf|date=2023-07-16}}" 6 May 2021 Zeng continued managing ATL after the acquisition together with Huang Shilin. TDK's acquisition saw ATL expand its production into the smartphone market, becoming a key battery supplier to prominent technology companies like Samsung and Apple. In 2006, ATL started exploring the [[electric vehicle]] (EV) battery market, with the first inquiry coming from Indian car company, [[REVA Electric Car Company|Reva]]. Given the fundamental differences between batteries used in EVs and those in portable devices, ATL's founders Zeng and Huang established a dedicated research department for EV battery development. In 2008, some of ATL's early EV batteries were used in a demo fleet of electric buses during the Beijing Olympics. This marked the company's first foray into the EV market. The electric-bus fleet formed part of a Chinese government demonstration programme to promote electrified transport. In 2011, Zeng and Huang separated ATL's EV battery business into a new company, [[CATL|Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Limited (CATL)]]. In the first quarter of 2020, the global smartphone battery cell market reached a total value of US$1.5 billion, a 5% year-over-year increase in revenue. ATL ranked first with a 36.5% revenue share, followed by [[LG Chem]] and [[Samsung SDI]], with the top three suppliers accounting for nearly 82% of market revenue.{{Cite web |date=2020-07-08 |title=ATL Leads the Global Smartphone Battery Market Share in 1Q20 |url=https://www.eetasia.com/atl-leads-the-global-smartphone-battery-market-share-in-1q20/ |website=EE Times Asia |language=en}} The growth was attributed to the adoption of higher-capacity and custom-designed lithium-ion polymer (Li-Po) cells by smartphone manufacturers. ATL supplied higher-capacity cells to leading smartphone OEMs. Later in 2020, the company expanded its operations to India by acquiring 180 acres of industrial land in [[Haryana]], aiming to supply batteries to the country's smartphone and EV industries. In September 2025, ATL's Indian subsidiary opened a lithium-ion battery cell manufacturing plant at Sohna, near [[Gurugram]] in Haryana, inaugurated by Union minister [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]].{{Cite web |date=2023-12-07 |title=Apple plans to move iPhone 16 battery production out of China and into India |url=https://qz.com/apple-plans-to-move-iphone-16-battery-production-out-of-1851079784 |access-date=2024-03-31 |website=Quartz |language=en}} The plant produces lithium-ion batteries for mobile phones, wearable and hearable devices, and laptops, and was planned to produce about 200 million battery packs annually at full capacity. Vaishnaw said this would meet roughly 40% of India's annual demand for mobile-phone battery packs.{{cite press release |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2163723®=48&lang=2 |title=Union Minister of Electronics and Information Technology Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw inaugurates State-of-the-art Advanced Lithium-ion Battery Plant in Sohna, Haryan |website=Ministry of Electronics & IT |location=India}} In 2023, ATL formed strategic partnerships with [[Group14 Technologies]] and AM Batteries. The partnership with Group14 Technologies aimed at integrating advanced [[Lithium–silicon battery|silicon battery]] technology to improve ATL's battery performance,{{Cite web |date=2023-02-28 |title=Group14 Technologies Enters Production to Power the Next Generation of Smartphones for Amperex Technology Limited (ATL) |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/group14-technologies-enters-production-to-power-the-next-generation-of-smartphones-for-amperex-technology-limited-atl-301757185.html |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}} while the collaboration with AM Batteries focused on developing solvent-free electrode manufacturing technology, addressing environmental concerns in the lithium-ion battery production industry.{{Cite web |date=2023-04-07 |title=AM Batteries and Amperex Technology Limited to jointly develop solvent-free electrode manufacturing technology for li-ion batteries |url=https://batteryindustry.tech/am-batteries-and-amperex-technology-limited-to-jointly-develop-solvent-free-electrode-manufacturing-technology-for-li-ion-batteries/ |website=BatteryIndustry.tech |language=en-GB}} ==Footprint== ATL is headquartered in Hong Kong, with subsidiaries in [[Ningde]] and [[Dongguan]], China,{{Cite web |title=ATL sued Zhuhai Guanyu for more than 100 million yuan! {{!}} Shanghai Non ferrous Metals |url=https://news.metal.com/newscontent/101730609/atl-sued-zhuhai-guanyu-for-more-than-100-million-yuan |access-date=2024-03-31 |website=news.metal.com}} as well as India. == Relationship with CATL == [[Huang Shilin]] co-founded ATL along with Zeng Yuqun in 1999, and would later become the vice chairman and Zeng's second in command at CATL.{{Cite web |last=Rathi |first=Akshat |date=October 12, 2023 |title=How China Left the World Far Behind in the Battery Race |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-10-12/how-china-left-the-world-far-behind-in-the-battery-race |website=Bloomberg}} CATL was formed in 2011 as a [[Spin-off (corporate)|spin-off]] of ATL's EV battery division.{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Alex |date=2022-12-20 |title=The History Of CATL: An Asian Giant {{!}} AceOn Group |url=https://www.aceongroup.com/news/the-history-of-catl-an-asian-giant/ |access-date=2024-03-31 |language=en-GB}} In 2021, [[Ampace]] was founded as a joint venture between ATL and CATL. The company is headquartered in [[Xiamen]]. While ATL has generally specialized in small batteries such as those used in smartphones and laptops, and CATL has specialized in large batteries used in EVs, Ampace has focused on medium sized batteries such as those used in electric scooters, [[Unmanned aerial vehicle|UAVs]], and power tools.{{Cite web |date=2024-04-18 |title=Little known spin-off of China's CATL dominates home energy storage market |url=https://www.scmp.com/business/china-business/article/3259342/how-little-known-spin-chinese-battery-giant-catl-has-come-dominate-global-home-energy-storage-market |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}} In April 2022, ATL and CATL partnered to establish a joint venture called the "Xiamen Ampcore Technology Limited" to further expand into the electric vehicles business. Xiamen Ampcore Technology Limited's capital is 5 billion RMB, with ATL having a 30% stake and CATL having a 70% stake. The same year, ATL and CATL also established a battery pack joint venture called "Xiamen Ampack Technology Limited" capital is RMB 1 billion, with ATL holding 70% and CATL holding 30%. ATL established Xiamen Ampeak Technology Limited, in which ATL owns 100% of the shares, as a holding company of the two joint ventures.{{Cite web |date=April 27, 2022 |title=Announcement on Business Alliance and Establishment of Joint Venture with Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited [Background to Disclosure] and Notice of Establishment of Subsidiary |url=https://www.tdk.com/en/news_center/press/20220427_02.html |website=TDK}} In January 2024, Ampace launched a [[battery management system]] (BMS) intended to improve safety and reliability in medium sized applications.{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Seth |date=2023-12-30 |title=Ampace: Pioneering Portable Power Solutions with Advanced Technology |url=https://wccftech.com/ampace-pioneering-portable-power-solutions-with-advanced-technology/ |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=Wccftech |language=en-US}} Other products developed by Ampace include the Andes 600 Pro, a 600 watt portable power station,{{Cite web |last=Westlake |first=Mark |title=Ampace Andes 600 Pro Portable Power Station Review - Gearbrain |url=https://www.gearbrain.com/ampace-andes-600-pro-review-2662304578.html |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=www.gearbrain.com |language=en}} and the Kunlun series ultra-long lifecycle batteries.{{Cite web |last=Sakharkar |first=Ashwini |date=2023-09-22 |title=Ampace unveils ultra-long cycle life batteries with 15,000-cycle |url=https://www.inceptivemind.com/ampace-unveils-ultra-long-cycle-life-batteries-15000-cycle/34351/ |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=Inceptive Mind |language=en-US}} == Relationship with TDK == [[TDK]] acquired ATL in 2005 for about US$100 million. ATL had been in financial difficulty before the acquisition.{{cite web |last=Wakayama |first=Takuya |date=2024-01-09 |script-title=ja:国産初のカセットテープからスマホ電池で世界首位のTDK株が人気の理由 |trans-title=Why TDK, the world's top smartphone-battery maker, is a popular stock |url=https://media.finasee.jp/articles/-/13037?page=2 |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=Finasee |language=ja}} ATL is a consolidated subsidiary of TDK, which holds a 100% equity stake in the company.{{cite press release |title=Announcement on acquisition of shares of a sub-subsidiary |date=2022-11-01 |publisher=TDK Corporation |url=https://www.tdk.com/en/news_center/press/20221101_01.html |access-date=2026-07-08}} It went on to become the largest supplier of smartphone batteries, and in the year to March 2023 it posted revenue above ¥500 billion and net profit above ¥90 billion. In 2022, TDK expanded ATL's business beyond smartphone batteries into medium-sized batteries for products such as electric scooters, residential energy-storage systems, and cellular base-station power supplies, with the goal of doubling its lithium-ion battery revenue over the following five years. It pursued this in part through joint ventures with CATL focused on mid-sized cells.{{cite news |last1=Mochizuki |first1=Takashi |last2=Furukawa |first2=Yuki |date=2022-01-06 |title=Apple Supplier TDK Looks Beyond Phones in Bid to Double Battery Sales |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-01-06/apple-supplier-tdk-looks-beyond-phones-to-double-battery-sales |access-date=2026-07-08 |work=Bloomberg}} ATL recorded approximately ¥740 billion (US$6.4 billion) in the year to March 2021, accounting for about half of TDK's revenue. TDK's 2024 medium-term business plan identified small rechargeable batteries for smartphones and personal computers as the core of its battery business, projecting an average annual growth rate of 2–3% for its battery and power-supply business through fiscal 2026 and planning about ¥320 billion of capital investment over the three years from fiscal 2024. The small batteries are made by ATL, which is pursuing higher energy density through high-value-added products such as cells using silicon-anode technology. Its main production bases are in China, but, citing geopolitical risk, production is also carried out in India, where a new plant in [[Haryana]] was scheduled to begin production in 2025.{{cite news |last=Abe |first=Misako |date=2024-06-18 |script-title=ja:高付加価値電池で攻勢かける、TDKの稼ぐ力の高め方 |trans-title=TDK goes on the offensive with high-value-added batteries |url=https://newswitch.jp/p/41936 |access-date=2026-07-08 |work=Newswitch |publisher=Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun |language=ja}} ATL began selling lithium-ion batteries with silicon anodes in 2023. Later versions stored more energy than comparable graphite-anode batteries, and TDK planned to begin mass production of third-generation silicon-anode cells in 2025, driven by the spread of artificial-intelligence features in mobile devices.{{cite news |date=2025-01-05 |title=iPhone Supplier TDK Rolls Out New Batteries to Keep Pace With AI |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-01-05/iphone-supplier-tdk-rolls-out-new-batteries-to-keep-pace-with-ai |access-date=2026-07-08 |work=Bloomberg}} TDK reported higher sales of small-capacity rechargeable batteries, ATL's main product line, in the fiscal year ended March 2026.{{cite web |date=2026-04-28 |title=FY March 2026 Full Year Performance Briefing (Speech Text) |url=https://www.tdk.com/en/ir/ir_events/conference/2026/4q_2.html |access-date=2026-07-08 |publisher=TDK Corporation}} In May 2026, TDK announced that its subsidiary Amperex Technology (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. would acquire 100% of the shares of Malaysia-based Linergy Power Sdn Bhd, making Linergy a wholly-owned subsidiary, as part of efforts to diversify battery production outside China.{{cite press release |title=Notice regarding the acquisition of shares in Linergy Power Sdn Bhd by our subsidiary (conversion into a wholly owned subsidiary) |date=2026-05-19 |publisher=TDK Corporation |url=https://www.tdk.com/en/news_center/press/20260519_00.html |access-date=2026-07-08}}{{cite news |date=2026-05-20 |title=Japan's TDK to buy Malaysia-based battery start-up for US$241.1 mil |url=https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/804307 |access-date=2026-07-08 |work=The Edge Malaysia}}{{cite news |author=Mars W. Mosqueda Jr. |date=2026-05-20 |title=TDK to acquire Malaysia's Linergy Power in $241m deal |url=https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/tdk-linergy-power-482856 |access-date=2026-07-08 |work=DealStreetAsia}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * {{official website|https://www.atlbattery.com/en/product.html}} [[Category:Battery manufacturers]] [[Category:Companies of Hong Kong]] [[Category:Chinese companies established in 1999]] [[Category:Electronics companies established in 1999]] [[Category:Chinese brands]]
extract:
Amperex Technology Limited (ATL) is a battery manufacturing company founded in 1999 by Robin Zeng. The company specializes in the research, development, and manufacturing of rechargeable lithium-ion and lithium-ion polymer batteries. ATL is notable for supplying batteries used in mobile devices, including smartphones, laptops, and digital cameras, sourcing their products to tech companies such as Apple and Samsung.
ATL is headquartered in Hong Kong and has production facilities in Dongguan and Ningde, China, as well as a lithium-ion battery cell plant in Haryana, India, opened in 2025.
